thresholds.source: UN-SPIDER & Twele et al. (2016) / Clement et al. (2018)
thresholds.exact_citation_or_algorithm: Twele, A., Cao, W., Plank, S., & Martinis, S. (2016). Automated flood mapping using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery. Applied Geography, 68, 65-74. Recommended standard: -3 dB backscatter drop due to specular water reflection.
thresholds.justification: Specular reflection on open flood water reduces C-band co-polarization backscatter by >= 3 dB relative to pre-flood land cover.

thresholds.derivation_method: Upper bound constraint to prevent false change on bright urban/rough terrain
thresholds.source: Martinis et al. (2015) / Twele et al. (2016)
thresholds.exact_citation_or_algorithm: Martinis, S., Kersten, J., & Twele, A. (2015). Towards automated Sentinel-1 flood processing. Remote Sensing, 7(10), 12534-12554. Upper bound of water backscatter rarely exceeds -14 dB in C-band.
thresholds.justification: Limits change detection to pixels whose final event backscatter is legitimately within the water-like radiometric domain (<= -14 dB).

thresholds.source: Data-derived from event scene distribution & Martinis et al. (2015)
thresholds.exact_citation_or_algorithm: Event scene 1st percentile = -16.47 dB; modal soil/vegetation = -8.09 dB. Threshold -15.5 dB sits at the bimodal valley between open calm water and low-vegetation soil.
thresholds.justification: Separates persistent and newly expanded standing water from damp agricultural soil.

thresholds.source: Twele et al. (2016) / Clement et al. (2018)
thresholds.exact_citation_or_algorithm: Cross-polarization VH backscatter over open water exhibits near-zero volume scattering and falls below -23.0 dB (approaching the C-SAR noise equivalent sigma zero NESZ).
thresholds.justification: Guarantees that detected water bodies lack vegetative volume scattering canopy.

thresholds.derivation_method: Topographic shadow & geometric distortion exclusion limit
thresholds.source: UN-SPIDER (2019) & Martinis et al. (2015) / Twele et al. (2016)
thresholds.exact_citation_or_algorithm: UN-SPIDER (2019) Recommended Practice: Radar-Based Flood Mapping. DEM slopes > 5 degrees generate radar shadowing and layover causing false-positive low backscatter.
thresholds.justification: Eliminates radar shadow artifacts on steep hillsides without impacting the flat alluvial river corridor (average river slope = 1.4 m/km = 0.08 deg).

thresholds.derivation_method: Multi-decadal historical surface water presence frequency threshold
thresholds.source: Pekel et al. (2016) / JRC Global Surface Water (v1.4)
thresholds.exact_citation_or_algorithm: Pekel, J. F., Cottam, A., Gorelick, N., & Belward, A. S. (2016). High-resolution mapping of global surface water and its long-term changes. Nature, 540(7633), 418-422. Occurrence >= 50% denotes historically recurrent water.
thresholds.justification: Defines historical recurrent water present >=50% of the 38-year Landsat observation record (1984–2021) to isolate new event flood expansion.
